sections.h2: Selling in Monroe Township, Middlesex County
sections.html: Monroe Township in Middlesex County, the ZIP 08831 township around Jamesburg, is a market defined by age-restricted communities and long Turnpike commutes. Population is about 49,830, up 2.4 percent since 2020. In the 2020 to 2024 survey 39.6 percent of residents were 65 or older and 91.1 percent of homes were owner occupied, a very high owner rate. The median owner value is $540,900 and median household income is $107,892. Mean travel to work is 40.3 minutes.

At 42.19 square miles, Monroe is the largest municipality in Middlesex County by total area, and it completely surrounds the borough of Jamesburg. The township turned suburban between 1960 and 1968, when Turnpike Exit 8A opened and the Rossmoor age-restricted community was developed. Many more followed, including Clearbrook, Concordia, Whittingham, Monroe Manor, Forsgate, Regency at Monroe, Stonebridge, The Ponds, Renaissance and Encore. Neighborhoods outside those are informal names such as Mill Lake Manor, Outcalt and Manor Heights.

If your house sits inside one of these communities, ask the association for its resale paperwork and any rules on who may buy, since the township's own forms say nothing about community rules.

sections.h2: Certificate of continued occupancy and permits
sections.html:
Ask the Construction Department whether your sale needs a certificate of continued occupancy. Chapter 39 of the township code lists one among its construction fees and carries the note "R-5 are optional," and R-5 is the use group for one and two family houses. The township's online forms page links out for construction applications.

Other forms a seller may touch:

  • A residential zoning permit, listed at a $25 fee, with commercial at $100.
  • A Tenancy Review Application and a Landlord Identity Registration for rented houses.
  • A Foreclosed Property Registration Form for vacant bank-owned homes.
  • Septic Site Evaluation and Well Application forms through the Health Department.

The fee chapter also notes that garden-type sheds of 200 square feet or less and 10 feet or less in height do not need a permit, and that roofing or siding on a detached one or two family house does not need one unless the siding is polypropylene. Ask the Construction Department for the permit history on the address before you list.

Buyers here trade commute time for space and age-restricted housing.

  • Roads: Turnpike Exit 8A, with a nine-lane toll gate, sits at the township's western edge. Route 32, Route 33 and a long list of county routes cross the township.
  • Bus: NJ Transit routes 138 and 139 run to the Port Authority Bus Terminal, and Coach USA Suburban Transit and Academy Bus provide weekday commuter service to the terminal and Wall Street.
  • Rail: the nearest stations are Metuchen, New Brunswick and Princeton Junction on the Northeast Corridor.
  • Local shuttle: a Middlesex County Area Transit line links Jamesburg and the New Brunswick station.

CentraState Healthcare System's hospital in Freehold Township serves the township, which matters to the many older buyers here.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and rate
sections.html:
Monroe tax bills are paid quarterly at the Tax Collector's office.

Quarterly tax due dates in Monroe Township.
QuarterDue date
FirstFebruary 1
SecondMay 1
ThirdAugust 1
FourthNovember 1

The township reported a 2022 general tax rate of 2.517 per $100 of assessed value, made up of county 0.461, school 1.470, municipal 0.489, county open space 0.039, municipal open space 0.015 and library 0.043. A fire district adds 0.135, 0.150 or 0.224 depending on whether the house is in District 1, 2 or 3, so check your bill for the district. Only 20 cents of each tax dollar goes to municipal operations and local open space, with school, county and fire district budgets making up roughly 80 percent.

The Assessor's forms page carries the senior and disability deduction, veteran's deduction, farmland assessment and the petition of appeal. For ANCHOR benefits, call the State Department of Treasury hotline at 1-888-238-1233.

Middlesex County follows the general state rule: petitions must be received by April 1, or May 1 where a municipal revaluation has taken place. The county Board of Taxation does not hold virtual hearings. Assessments above $1,000,000 can go directly to the State Tax Court.

The seller pays the state Realty Transfer Fee at recording, and the amount climbs with the price in bands, so ask your closing agent for the figure at your contract price.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in New Brunswick
sections.html: The Middlesex County Clerk records deeds at 75 Bayard Street, 4th floor, New Brunswick, from 8:30 am to 4:10 pm on weekdays, and you must arrive by 4 pm. Appointments are not required but are served first. A paper deed needs original signatures with printed names, the words "Prepared by," the tax block, lot and consideration, and a record and return address. A paper cover sheet is required, and leaving it off adds a $20 indexing charge. E-recordings are an alternative and skip the cover sheet.

Start with the Construction Department. Ask whether a certificate of continued occupancy applies to your house and request the permit history, so any open permit is closed before a buyer's attorney finds it. If the house is rented, file the tenancy and landlord forms. If it is vacant and bank-owned, the foreclosed property registration applies.

For a house inside an age-restricted community, contact the association early and learn who may buy, because that rule shrinks the buyer pool and can slow a traditional listing. A cash purchase from a buyer who qualifies under the community rules can skip the mortgage appraisal and a long wait for an approval.

Gather what a buyer's side will ask for: the tax bill showing your fire district, any deductions you receive such as the senior or veteran deduction, and the permit history. Deductions do not always carry over to a new owner, so the Assessor's office can tell you what changes after the deed is recorded. Before closing, confirm which tax quarter is next, since the buyer's attorney will prorate it. Have the deed prepared with the required wording and the cover sheet, or ask whether e-recording is available. Allow time to reach New Brunswick before the clerk's cutoff on closing day, and ask the closing attorney whether the deed will be filed on paper or electronically.

faqs.q: Does Monroe Township in Middlesex County require a resale certificate?
faqs.a: Ask the Construction Department. The township fee chapter lists a certificate of continued occupancy and marks R-5 one and two family houses as optional, so a sale may not need one.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline for a Monroe assessment in Middlesex County?
faqs.a: April 1, or May 1 in a year the municipality was revalued. Middlesex follows the general state rule, and the petition must be received by the county board by that date.

faqs.q: When are Monroe Township property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1 at the Tax Collector's office. The township's fire district adds a separate rate depending on whether the home is in District 1, 2 or 3.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Monroe sale?
faqs.a: The Middlesex County Clerk in New Brunswick records it. Bring original signatures, a Prepared by line, block, lot and consideration, plus a paper cover sheet to avoid the $20 indexing charge.

faqs.q: What should I know if my Monroe house is in an age-restricted community?
faqs.a: Ask the association for its resale paperwork and any rules on who may buy. The township's own forms do not cover community rules, so the association is the place to check.
